preamble: The voiceless retroflex stop [ʈ] is lenited to the voiced retroflex flap [ɽ] between vowels. In Tamil, voicing is not contrastive in native vocabulary, and a single (non-geminate) retroflex obstruent written ட is realized between vowels as either a voiced stop [ɖ] or a flap [ɽ], while the voiceless stop [ʈ(ː)] is kept for the orthographic geminate ட்ட. The flap is the more lenited end of the intervocalic weakening that Tamil applies to all its single stops.

examples.note: Single intervocalic ṭ realized as a flap; Wiktionary transcribes the voiced-stop variant [näːɖɯ].

examples.to: voiced stop or flap, contrasting with geminate பட்டு paṭṭu [paʈːɯ] 'silk'
examples.note: Keane (2004): for retroflex sounds either a voiced stop or a flap is found between vowels; the geminate stays a voiceless stop.

sources: Keane, E. (2004). Tamil. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 34(1), 111–116. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100304001549
